source_document_supplied_by_user.description: Official English text of UAE Federal Law No. 10 of 2015 Concerning Food Safety (22 articles).
source_document_supplied_by_user.status: used as base; all substantive content re-verified against current official and secondary sources

verification.method: Text extracted from the supplied PDF, then each legal instrument, authority name and requirement cross-checked against official gazettes/legal portals, the competent authority website, FAOLEX/ECOLEX, and current regulatory-intelligence reporting.
caveats: Federal Law No. 10 of 2015 remains the primary federal food safety law and has NOT been repealed as of the compile date.

MOCCAE publicly announced a package of new food safety legislation (including a National System for Control and Inspection of Imported Food) targeted for early 2025; issuance had not been confirmed in the official gazette at the compile date. Treat as pending.
Emirate-level requirements (Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, Ajman, RAK, Fujairah, UAQ) sit on top of the federal law and differ in detail; always check the relevant local authority.

primary_federal.name: Ministry of Climate Change and Environment
primary_federal.role: Federal competent authority for food safety under Federal Law No. 10/2015. Sets federal policy, technical regulations, food/fodder import controls, national food safety strategy, and coordinates the National Food Safety Committee.

coordination_body.name: National Food Safety Committee
coordination_body.role: Federal-local coordination on food safety policy, harmonising inspection regimes across the seven emirates.

standards_body.name: Ministry of Industry and Advanced Technology - Standards and Metrology sector (formerly ESMA)
standards_body.role: National standards, technical regulations, conformity assessment, Emirates Conformity Assessment Scheme (ECAS) and the national halal scheme (UAE.S GSO 2055 series).
standards_body.outdated_reference_note: Federal Law No. 10/2015 cites Federal Law No. 28 of 2001 establishing the Emirates Authority for Standardization and Metrology (ESMA). ESMA was abolished in 2020 and its mandate transferred to MOIAT. Any reference to 'ESMA' in the 2015 text should now be read as MOIAT.

local_authorities.name: Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority
local_authorities.note: Operates a Risk-Based inspection System (RBS) for food establishments; cited as a model for the planned national system.

local_authorities.name: Dubai Municipality - Food Safety Department
local_authorities.note: Food label/product registration and establishment grading (Food Watch / FIRS platforms).

local_authorities.name: Sharjah City Municipality - Public Health Department

supporting_authorities.name: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP) / local customs authorities
Emirates Authority for Halal (national halal scheme under MOIAT)
supporting_authorities.role: Recognition of halal certification bodies and halal national mark.

executive_regulations.citation: Cabinet Resolution No. 26 of 2017 on the Executive Regulations of Federal Law No. 10 of 2015 Concerning Food Safety
executive_regulations.content: Detailed rules on food establishment obligations, registration/notification, hygiene, HACCP-based controls, import/export procedures, traceability, recall, inspection, grievance and conciliation procedures.

regional_body.name: GCC Standardization Organization
regional_body.arabic_name: هيئة التقييس لدول مجلس التعاون لدول الخليج العربية
regional_body.role: Regional standards body for the six GCC states plus Yemen. Issues GSO standards and GCC technical regulations which member states adopt as national standards, generally making them mandatory for food placed on the market.
regional_body.note: Adoption is national: a GSO standard becomes legally binding in a member state only once that state's standards body/competent authority adopts it (as a national standard or via a national technical regulation).

key_standards.title: Labelling of prepackaged food stuffs
key_standards.note: Core GCC horizontal labelling standard. Requires Arabic labelling (other languages alongside Arabic), name of food, ingredient list, nutrition information, net contents, name/address of manufacturer/packer/importer, country of origin, date marking, storage and use instructions, and declaration of the 13 GCC allergen categories.

key_standards.title: Expiration dates for food products - Part 1: Mandatory expiration periods
key_standards.note: Applies to perishable foods (milk/milk products, eggs, meat, poultry, fish, crustaceans, infant foods, ready-to-eat foods, fresh table eggs) chilled at 0-5 C.

key_standards.title: Expiration dates for food products - Part 2: Voluntary expiration periods
key_standards.note: Frozen products held at <= -18 C, certain non-perishable chilled products (0-5 C) and ambient products stored in ventilated stores at <= 25 C. Products outside the standard require expiry periods agreed with the competent authority on a scientific basis.

key_standards.title: Food additives permitted for use in foodstuffs
key_standards.note: Positive list. Only additives with a JECFA ADI (or otherwise assessed as safe) and a Codex INS number are eligible. Replaced/consolidated earlier GSO additive standards.

key_standards.title: Permitted sweeteners in foodstuffs
key_standards.note: Sweeteners not permitted in infant and children's foods. Label warnings required for aspartame (phenylketonuria), sucralose (<=25 C), and laxative-effect warnings for polyols (sorbitol >40 g/day, mannitol >20 g/day, xylitol >40 g/day, lactitol, maltitol, erythritol).

key_standards.title: General principles of food hygiene
Hygienic regulations for food plants and their personnel
key_standards.note: 1984 base standard; still cited by national codes of practice.

key_standards.title: General requirements for transportation and storage of chilled and frozen foods
Stores for frozen and chilled foodstuff - Part 2: General requirements
Requirements for handling of ready-to-eat foods
Hygienic conditions for school canteens and handled food
General requirements for food shops and establishments
Halal food - Part 1: General requirements
key_standards.note: 2015 edition is the operative version. A draft revision GSO 2055-1:2026 was released for public consultation on 2026-02-17 (comment deadline 2026-04-18) tightening supply-chain, certification and labelling rules. Treat GSO 2055-1:2015 as in force and GSO 2055-1:2026 as pending until formally adopted.

key_standards.title: Halal food - Part 2: General requirements for halal certification bodies
Halal food - Part 3: General requirements for accreditation bodies accrediting halal certification bodies
Microbiological criteria for foodstuffs
Maximum limits of pesticide residues in agricultural and food products
Contaminants and toxins in food and feed
key_standards.note: GSO 2481 mirrors Codex GSCTFF for heavy metals and mycotoxins. Verify latest edition in the GSO standards store before use.

key_standards.title: Requirements of nutritional labelling
Food packaging - general requirements for food contact materials
key_standards.note: Food-contact material requirements are largely GSO-harmonised across the six states.

codex.note: All six GCC states are Codex members; GSO standards are predominantly Codex-aligned, and national laws routinely allow Codex to be used where no GSO/national standard exists.

food_business_requirements.establishment_licensing: Trade licence from the relevant economic department plus a food establishment permit from the local municipality/food authority of the emirate. Federal law requires all establishments in the food chain (including free zones) to comply.
food_business_requirements.food_safety_management_system: HACCP-based system required for food establishments; Dubai and Abu Dhabi mandate documented HACCP or an equivalent certified FSMS for most categories.
food_business_requirements.person_in_charge: Designated Person in Charge (PIC) / food safety supervisor with accredited training is required by Dubai Municipality and ADAFSA.
food_business_requirements.food_handler_requirements: Occupational health card / food handler health certificate and basic food hygiene training; renewal periods set locally.
food_business_requirements.traceability: One-step-back / one-step-forward records mandatory (Law 10/2015 Art. 7 and Cabinet Res. 26/2017).
food_business_requirements.recall: Mandatory withdrawal/recall and notification to the competent authority (Art. 8).

product_registration_and_label_approval.description: Food product and label registration is required before marketing. At federal level MOCCAE operates the ZAD digital platform for food import/registration workflows; Dubai Municipality operates its own food label registration (FIRS/Food Watch) and Abu Dhabi via ADAFSA. First-time importers of a product generally need prior approval before the consignment arrives.

labelling.language: Arabic mandatory; English or another language may appear alongside Arabic and must be identical in content.
mandatory_particulars: Full ingredient list in descending order
Additives by common name or E-number
Storage conditions and instructions for use
labelling.date_marking_rules: Day-Month-Year for shelf life under 3 months; Month-Year permitted for shelf life over 3 months. Dates must be printed, embossed or stamped by the producer in indelible ink on the original pack. Stickers for production/expiry dates are not permitted, and only one production and one expiry date may appear.
labelling.animal_origin_disclosure: Source of animal-derived ingredients (e.g. gelatin, lecithin, mono- and di-glycerides) must be declared.
prohibited: Misleading descriptions or false claims (Law 10/2015 Art. 12 and Art. 14(3))
Health claims not permitted under the applicable technical regulation
Artificial sweeteners and non-permitted nutrients in infant/children's foods

additives_contaminants_and_residues.additives: GSO 2500 positive list; sweeteners per GSO 995 with mandatory label warnings.
additives_contaminants_and_residues.contaminants: GSO/Codex-aligned maximum limits for heavy metals and mycotoxins.
additives_contaminants_and_residues.pesticide_mrls: GSO 1863 MRLs; Codex used as fallback.
additives_contaminants_and_residues.irradiation_and_gmo: Irradiated foods and GM-containing foods must be declared on the label; check current MOIAT technical regulations for thresholds.

mandatory_for: Meat and poultry and their products
Products containing animal-derived ingredients (gelatin, enzymes, emulsifiers, rennet, etc.)
halal_requirements.scheme: UAE National Halal Scheme / Emirates Halal Mark administered under MOIAT; halal certificates must be issued by a certification body accredited/recognised under the scheme.
halal_requirements.pork_and_alcohol: Trading food containing pork, pork derivatives, alcohol, or anything contrary to Sharia without a licence is a criminal offence (Art. 14(2)). Licensed pork/alcohol sections are permitted in designated outlets with segregation and clear labelling.

pre_import: Importer must hold a valid trade licence with food import activity
Product/label registration and, for first-time products, prior MOCCAE or local-authority approval
Registration on the applicable federal/local digital platform
documents: Health/veterinary/phytosanitary certificate from the exporting country's competent authority where applicable
Halal slaughter certificate for meat and poultry; halal certificate for products with halal-relevant ingredients
Analysis certificates where required by risk category
Bill of lading / airway bill and customs declaration
import_clearance.border_control: Risk-based inspection at points of entry with documentary, identity and physical checks; sampling and laboratory analysis for higher-risk categories.
import_clearance.free_zones: Law 10/2015 Art. 19 expressly extends the law to free zones.
import_clearance.shelf_life_on_arrival: GCC practice requires a substantial proportion of shelf life remaining on arrival (commonly at least half for short-shelf-life goods; category-specific rules apply). Confirm the exact figure with the receiving authority for the specific product.
import_clearance.non_compliance: Detention, re-export or destruction at importer's cost; administrative and criminal measures under Arts. 14 and 17.

criminal_penalties_article_14.offence: Trading adulterated, harmful or spoiled food at any stage of the food chain
criminal_penalties_article_14.penalty: Imprisonment not less than 3 months and/or fine of AED 100,000 to AED 2,000,000

criminal_penalties_article_14.offence: Trading without licence any food containing pork meat/derivatives/products, alcoholic substances, or any material contrary to Islamic Sharia
criminal_penalties_article_14.penalty: Imprisonment not less than 1 month and/or fine of AED 50,000 to AED 500,000

criminal_penalties_article_14.offence: Trading, circulating or publishing a false description of food to mislead consumers
Disposing of food or fodder held under official custody
criminal_penalties_article_14.penalty: Imprisonment 3 months to 2 years and/or fine of AED 100,000 to AED 300,000

criminal_penalties_article_14.offence: Trading food or fodder contrary to technical regulations issued under the Law
Attempt to commit any offence under the Law
criminal_penalties_article_14.penalty: Same penalty as the completed offence

criminal_penalties_article_14.offence: Any other breach of the Law not specifically penalised
criminal_penalties_article_14.penalty: Fine of not less than AED 10,000
Penalty is doubled in all cases

administrative_measures_article_17: Administrative closure for up to 3 months (may be lifted early once the breach is removed)
Final closure and request to withdraw the licence if the breach is not remedied
enforcement_and_penalties.grievance: Establishment may challenge a temporary or permanent closure decision within 30 days of notification, per the Executive Regulations.
enforcement_and_penalties.conciliation: Settlement is available for the offences in Art. 14(2), (5) and (7) before referral to court, for up to AED 100,000 per offence; Cabinet sets the conciliation schedule.
enforcement_and_penalties.prosecution_gate: Criminal action for Art. 14(2), (5) and (7) offences requires a written request from the Ministry or the competent authority.

recent_developments.item: MOCCAE announced a package of new food safety legislation and a unified national control and inspection system, expected from early 2025.
recent_developments.status: Issuance not confirmed in the official gazette at compile date

recent_developments.item: GSO released draft GSO 2055-1:2026 revising halal food general requirements (consultation to 2026-04-18).

outdated_items_found_in_supplied_pdf: ESMA (Federal Law 28/2001) cited in the preamble no longer exists; functions moved to MOIAT in 2020.
Ministry of Environment and Water (proposing minister) has been renamed the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE).

Preamble references to the 1987 Penal Code, 1992 Criminal Procedure Law, 1992 Trademarks Law, 1984 Commercial Companies Law and 2006 Consumer Protection Law have all been superseded by 2020-2022 decree-laws.
The printed Hijri date '21 Muharram 1427 AH' in the English PDF does not correspond to 3 November 2015; the correct Hijri equivalent is 21 Muharram 1437 AH.
